R9954.summary: Diego López de Ayala, Cisneros's agent at Charles's court in Brussels, reports that offices in Castile are sold at court to unworthy men and granted from Flanders over the regent's head, on the Arévalo and Málaga affairs and the power over the military Orders, and that peace (probably with France) is concluded and the king resolved to embark from Zeeland. reading.txt is the project's reading; the two print files are the 1849 Simancas decipherment as printed by Gayangos and de la Fuente (1875), split into Cartas XLIX and LIV.
R9954.en:
AGS 0002

As to the offices that are vacant in these kingdoms, and the drawbacks of their being filled from here with persons
who sell them to base men, His Highness says that this will be looked to closely from now on. People say that Your
Lordship fills all of them, and His Highness hardly any; so let Your Lordship do there as well what you advise here;
certainly they would see that none was filled there, and so His Highness writes.

The offices that His Highness has given and promised, as far as I know, are these: to the Marquis of Villena a
regidorship of Toledo that was Baeza's; to Rodrigo Niño another of Plasencia; and this one ⟨is known? — ciphertext
"rabese"⟩ here that Your Lordship gave to a nephew of Carvajal;

system: Simple substitution of invented signs for Spanish letters, with a few name and word signs (Xebres, que).
